title: Halting during edge-list membership check
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w,E$ be bit strings, and let $o$ be an oracle on bit strings. Suppose that on every encoding of a natural number $p$, the oracle returns the $p$th bit of $E$, defaulting to false beyond the end of $E$; suppose also that the input formed from $n$ and $w$ has edge target $(iv,tv)$. If $E$ has length at most $B$, then for every register state $p,c,a$ and suffix $r$ such that $E$ after position $p$ consists of the encoded list $as$ followed by $r$, and $c,a\le B$, the edge-scanning machine started at its argument-list scan state halts with answer true exactly when $iv$ occurs in $as$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle answers on encoded natural numbers equal the corresponding E bit, defaulting to false
E.drop p equals the encoding of as followed by rest
